events.title: First Battle of Bull Run
events.description: Union and Confederate armies fought near Manassas, Virginia, in the first major land battle of the American Civil War. Many Washington spectators had come out expecting an easy Union victory. Instead, the Confederates won and the Union troops retreated in disarray.
events.significance: The battle ended hopes of a short war and showed both sides that the conflict would be long and costly.

events.title: Birth of Ernest Hemingway
events.description: Ernest Hemingway was born in Oak Park, Illinois. He became one of the most influential American novelists of the 20th century. His spare, direct prose shaped modern fiction.
events.significance: His works include The Old Man and the Sea. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954.

events.title: First Human Steps on the Moon
events.description: Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon after Apollo 11 landed. The moonwalk took place early on July 21 in Universal Time. It was still the evening of July 20 in the United States. Millions of people watched on live television.
events.significance: The moonwalk was the high point of the space race and a landmark in human achievement.

events.title: Coldest Temperature Ever Recorded on Earth
events.description: Russia's Vostok Station in Antarctica measured about −89.2 °C (−128.6 °F). This is the lowest air temperature ever recorded on Earth.
events.significance: The reading still stands as the planet's record low. It shows how extreme the Antarctic interior is.
